title: Airline-card page accepts expiry years above 2099
summary: The airline-card page sends expiry years above 2099, which the API refuses after a round trip. The page checks only that the year is at least 2000 and not past, but the contract caps `expiryYear` at 2099, so the API answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` and the page empties every input. A 400 is not a decline, so no attempt is counted.
reproduce: Book with the airline card up to `/checkout/pay-airline.html`.
Type `4111 1111 1111 1111`, month 12, year 2100, code 123 and a valid name, then press **Pay €…**.
expected: A field error before anything is sent, with the values kept (as for other card errors).
actual: The completion is sent and answers 400. The page shows “Enter the expiry month (MM) and year (YYYY) of the card” and every input is empty.
fix: In `cardProblems` also refuse `card.expiryYear > 2099` with `TEXT.errorExpiry`.

title: OTA default cabin (search_defaults) never applies on the hosted storefront
summary: A default cabin set for the OTA has no effect on its own storefront. The server applies `storefront_settings.search_defaults.cabin` only to searches sent without a cabin, but the storefront form always sends one, with Economy preselected, and `StorefrontConfig` publishes no search defaults.
reproduce: Set `storefront_settings.search_defaults = '{"cabin":"BUSINESS"}'` for the OTA (development only) and drop the `t:<tenantId>:test:sf:*` cache keys.
Open `http://localhost:5173/`, look at **Cabin**, then search.
expected: Business preselected, or the search uses the OTA's default.
actual: Economy is preselected and sent.
fix: A product decision: publish the default cabin in `StorefrontConfig` and preselect it in the form, or have the form leave the cabin out unless the traveller changes it.

title: Card holder name limited to ASCII, with no hint to drop accents
summary: A card holder name with accents is refused with no hint why. Holder names must match `^[A-Za-z .'-]{2,64}$` on the page and `^[A-Za-z .'-]+$` in the contract (Amadeus sends them in upper case), so “José Müller” gets “Enter the name as it is written on the card”.
reproduce: On `/checkout/pay-airline.html` type the name `José Müller` with a valid card and press **Pay €…**.
expected: The traveller is told to type the name without accents, or the accents are converted.
actual: The error is “Enter the name as it is written on the card”.
fix: Extend `errorHolder` with “use Latin letters without accents”, or convert accents (NFD, then strip combining marks) before checking.

title: Currency change gives no visible feedback
summary: Sighted users get no sign that a currency change applies only from the next search. Choosing another currency stores it, swaps the client and writes “Prices will be shown in {currency} from your next search” to the visually hidden live region only; the prices stay as they were. This follows README §7 and WCAG 3.2.2, so the owner decides whether a visible note is wanted.
reproduce: Give the OTA two supported currencies.
Search MAD → PAR on `http://localhost:5173` and change the header currency on the results page.
expected: A visible hint that the next search uses the new currency.
actual: Only the select changes; prices stay in the old currency, with no visible message.
fix: Show a small visible status next to the selector or above the results, with the live region's text.

title: Sign-up “Check your e-mail” branch is dead; the docs promise it
summary: The docs say sign-up shows “Check your e-mail” when verification is required; the code always opens a session. The API never answers `emailVerification.policy = required_before_sign_in`, so with `require_email_verification` on the customer is signed in at once and is stopped only at checkout. The code is consistent; the flow doc and `pages-account.md` are wrong.
reproduce: In the OTA admin turn on “require e-mail verification” (`storefront_settings.require_email_verification = true`).
Open `http://localhost:5173/account/sign-up.html` and create an account.
expected: Per the docs: “Check your e-mail” and no session.
actual: The page goes to `/account/` signed in (“Hi, <name>”). Checkout later answers `403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`, and the price page shows “Verify your e-mail address to book”.
fix: Correct `ota/docs/flows/my-bookings-and-guest-lookup.md` §3 step 1 and the sign-up row of `ota/frontend/docs/pages-account.md` §5: a session always opens, and verification blocks only checkout. Keep the defensive branch.

title: /queues lists only the queues present in the newest 100 snapshots
summary: A queue drops off `/queues` once 100 newer snapshots exist, although its snapshots are kept 30 days. The overview groups only the newest 100 `queue_snapshots` rows by office, queue and category. With up to 20 monitored queues per connection polled every 15 minutes (80 rows an hour), a queue read by staff drops off within about 75 minutes.
reproduce: Sign in to the console as owner, test environment.
`/queues` → open queue 5, category 0 → **Read now from Amadeus** once.
Open queue 6 and press **Read now from Amadeus** 100 times (or reload `/queues/6?read=1` 100 times).
Open `/queues`.
expected: Queue 5 is still listed with its last read time.
actual: Only the queues in the newest 100 rows are listed; queue 5 is gone until someone reads it again.
fix: Give `consoleListQueueSnapshots` a “latest per queue” mode (`DISTINCT ON (office_id, queue_id, category) … ORDER BY fetched_at DESC`) and use it on `/queues`, or page through `listSnapshots` until the distinct queues are complete.

title: /shopping misses the default markup rule after 500 rules
summary: With 500 or more markup rules ahead of it, the default rule is reported missing. The orientation tile looks for `isDefault` in at most 5 pages of 100 rules, listed in evaluation order, and the default rule has priority 1000, so the tile says “This OTA has no default markup rule.” Prices are not affected.
reproduce: As owner, create 500 markup rules with priority below 1000 (a script calling `createMarkupRule`, or development-only SQL inserts into `tenant_<key>.markup_rules`).
Open `/shopping`.
expected: The tile names the default rule and its percentage.
actual: “This OTA has no default markup rule.”
fix: Add an `isDefault` filter to `consoleListMarkupRules` (or a get-default operation) and read the rule with limit 1.

title: OTA admin README says to open the demo OTA's console, which has no owner
summary: The OTA admin README sends developers to the demo OTA's console, which no account can open. README §12 says “portal on 3000: sign in, pick the demo OTA, Open console”, but neither dev seed gives the demo OTA a member. The e2e README says it plainly: “The demo OTA is no one's”.
reproduce: Run both `dev:seed` commands and `pnpm dev`.
Sign up in the portal and look for the demo OTA under your OTAs: it is not there, so there is no **Open console** for it.
expected: The README path works, or it says to create your own OTA.
actual: The demo OTA is listed for no account.
fix: In `ota/admin/README.md` line 313 write: “portal on 3000: sign up, create your own OTA at `/otas/new`, wait until Active, Open console (the demo OTA has no owner)”.

title: Traveller date checks use the UTC day, not the OTA's time zone
summary: A date of birth or document issue date that is today for the traveller can be refused as being in the future. `setTravelers` passes `today = utcDate(now)`, so in a time zone ahead of UTC, between local midnight and UTC midnight, the local today is still tomorrow in UTC. Expiry is not affected: a document that expires before the last flight is refused anyway.
reproduce: Set the OTA's time zone to `Asia/Tokyo` (OTA admin storefront settings, or `UPDATE tenant_<key>.storefront_settings SET time_zone = 'Asia/Tokyo'`, development only).
Between 00:00 and 09:00 Tokyo time, open a checkout and `PUT /v1/checkouts/{id}/travelers` with a document whose `issuanceDate` is today's Tokyo date (or an infant born today).
expected: Accepted: the date is today for the traveller and the OTA.
actual: `422 TRAVELER_DATA_INVALID` with “The issue date cannot be in the future.” (or “The date of birth cannot be in the future.”).
fix: Compute today in the OTA's `storefront_settings.time_zone` for the “not in the future” checks, or compare with the latest calendar date on Earth (UTC+14) so no real local today is refused.

title: Stripe dummy keys of .env.example count as configured: card offered, payment fails with 502
summary: The dummy Stripe keys of `.env.example` count as configured: the card method is offered and payment fails with 502. After the documented `cp .env.example .env.local`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_TEST=sk_test_replace_me` and `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY_TEST=pk_test_replace_me` pass the key patterns, so `storefront.get` offers the card method with the dummy publishable key and `checkout.createPayment` fails at Stripe with `502 PAYMENT_PROVIDER_ERROR`. README §4 says that without keys the storefront offers no payment method; the e2e harness already treats the dummies as unset.
reproduce: `cp ota/backend/.env.example ota/backend/.env.local` without editing the Stripe lines; start the API.
`curl -H 'X-Api-Key: pk_test_…' http://localhost:4000/v1/storefront | jq .payment`
Open a checkout and `POST /v1/checkouts/{id}/payments` with `{"method":"card"}`.
expected: No card method (or a clear `424 PAYMENT_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED`), as README §4 says for missing keys.
actual: `payment.supportedMethods` contains `card` with publishable key `pk_test_replace_me`; `createPayment` answers `502 PAYMENT_PROVIDER_ERROR`.
fix: Leave the two `STRIPE_*_KEY_TEST` lines (and the `whsec` dummies) empty in `.env.example` with a comment, or treat values ending in `_replace_me` as unset in `config.ts`, as the e2e harness does. Align README §4.

title: OpenAPI examples use a 6-character booking reference (VX9M4T)
summary: The contract's examples show a 6-character booking reference (`VX9M4T`); real ones have 8. Every booking reference the code creates (checkout and PNR import) is `VX` plus 6 characters, but the examples (`CheckoutCompletion`, the `lookupBooking` request and answer) show `VX9M4T`. An SDK user who copies the example, or validates references against it, is misled.
reproduce: Open the `lookupBooking` example in the contract and compare it with the reference of any booking in `tenant_demo.bookings`.
expected: Examples show a real-format reference such as `VX9M4TQ7`.
actual: Examples show `VX9M4T` (6 characters).
fix: Replace `VX9M4T` with an 8-character reference (for example `VX9M4TQ7`) in the three examples and in `ota/docs/flows/my-bookings-and-guest-lookup.md` line 49.

title: dev-seed comment says console.bookings.create is checked against the staff role
summary: A dev-seed comment says `console.bookings.create` is checked against the staff role; no check happens. The operation is deferred: its route carries only `PENDING_OPERATION` metadata, so the staff, scope and permission guards (which read `OPENAPI_OPERATION`) let it through, and any caller with a valid credential gets `501`.
reproduce: Sign in to the console as a viewer and call `POST /v1/console/bookings` (or `console.bookings.create` in the SDK).
expected: The comment matches the behaviour.
actual: `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` for every role, with no permission check.
fix: Reword the comment: `console.bookings.create` is a deferred route that answers 501 without any role or permission check.

title: Contract says finance may add booking notes; the API refuses them
summary: The contract says finance may add booking notes; the API refuses them. `consoleAddBookingNote`'s description says “Permission `bookings:write` (finance may also add notes)”, but `x-permission` is `bookings:write` and the finance role does not hold it, so a finance member gets `403 FORBIDDEN` (and the OTA admin hides the form).
reproduce: Invite a finance member in the portal, open the console as that member, and call `POST /v1/console/bookings/{id}/notes` (or try the note form).
expected: Description and behaviour agree.
actual: `403 FORBIDDEN` with `details.requiredPermission = bookings:write`, and a denied `staff_actions` row.
fix: Remove “(finance may also add notes)” from the description; the role matrix is decided in OADR-0011 and scope §1.3.

title: A throwing custom fetch is reported as NETWORK_ERROR and retried
summary: A synchronous throw from a custom `fetch` (a programming error) is reported as `NETWORK_ERROR` and retried. `fetchFn(url, init)` runs inside the `try`, so the throw lands in the same `catch` as network failures and is retried up to `maxRetries` times. An async `TypeError` cannot be told from a network failure (the Fetch standard uses `TypeError` for both); a synchronous throw can.
reproduce: In Node: `createVelexisClient({ publishableKey: 'pk_test_x', baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:4000', fetch: () => { throw new Error('bug') } }).storefront.get()`, and count the calls to the fake `fetch`.
expected: The programming error is rethrown, or reported without retries.
actual: Three calls, then `ConnectionError NETWORK_ERROR` with the original error as `cause`.
fix: Call `fetchFn` in its own `try` before the race, and rethrow a synchronous throw as it is (or as an error that is not retried).

title: request() escape hatch accepts “.” and “..” path segments
summary: The `request()` escape hatch lets a path leave the base URL with `..`. It refuses `//`, `#`, whitespace and backslashes but not dot segments, while `fillPath` refuses `.` and `..` in method parameters. With `baseUrl: '/api'`, `request('GET', '/../v1/storefront')` goes to `/v1/storefront` on the same origin, outside the `/api` prefix (with cookies in cookie mode).
reproduce: In a storefront unit test call `client.request('GET', '/../v1/storefront')` and look at the URL the fake `fetch` receives: `/api/../v1/storefront`, which the browser resolves to `/v1/storefront`.
expected: `TypeError`: the request path must not contain `.` or `..` segments.
actual: The request is sent to a path outside the base.
fix: In `request()`, refuse a path whose segments include `.` or `..` (also percent-encoded, `%2e`).

title: Idempotency-Key passed in options.headers skips the 16–128 character check
summary: A short `Idempotency-Key` passed as a header is sent, and the API refuses it. `idempotencyKeyOf` takes `options.idempotencyKey`, else an `Idempotency-Key` header, else a UUID, but only `options.idempotencyKey` goes through the 16 to 128 visible-ASCII check.
reproduce: `client.checkout.create({ pricedOfferId: 'prc_…' }, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'short' } })` against the local API.
expected: A `TypeError` before any request, as for `{ idempotencyKey: 'short' }`.
actual: The request goes out and the API answers 400.
fix: Validate an `Idempotency-Key` found in `options.headers` (or the client's headers) with the same rule in `validateRequestOptions`.

title: A client with no key, or with a hostingKey, is accepted but every call fails
summary: A client with no key, or with a `hostingKey`, is created without complaint, but every call fails with 401. `sessionModeOf` answers `token` when no key is given, so the client sends no `X-Api-Key`; a `hostingKey` makes a server-mode client, but the MVP API refuses every `hk_` key with `401 INVALID_API_KEY`.
reproduce: From `ota/sdk`: `node -e "import('@velexis/ota-sdk').then(async m=>{const c=m.createVelexisClient({baseUrl:'http://127.0.0.1:4000'});try{await c.storefront.get()}catch(e){console.log(e.status,e.code)}})"`
expected: A `TypeError` at construction saying a key is needed, or a README note.
actual: Construction succeeds and the call answers 401.
fix: Document it in README §4 (no key means token mode without `X-Api-Key`; `hostingKey` is not served in the MVP), or throw a `TypeError` when no key is given and the session is not `cookie`.

title: ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED never reaches browser callers; they see NETWORK_ERROR
summary: Browsers never see `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`: they get `NETWORK_ERROR` after retries. The key check refuses an unlisted origin with 403 before CORS headers are added, so the browser hides the answer; `fetch` rejects, the SDK reports `ConnectionError NETWORK_ERROR` and retries GETs twice. The JSDoc `@throws PermissionError ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` holds only for callers outside a browser.
reproduce: Serve a page from `http://127.0.0.1:8080` that calls `createVelexisClient({ publishableKey: <seeded pk_test_ key>, baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:4000' }).storefront.get()`.
Watch the console and the Network tab.
expected: `PermissionError ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, as the JSDoc says.
actual: A CORS error, three refused requests and `ConnectionError NETWORK_ERROR`.
fix: Add `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to the `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` refusal (it reveals nothing about the key), or say in the JSDoc and the README that browsers see `NETWORK_ERROR`.

title: Card numbers in free text that arrives from Amadeus are stored as received
summary: Free text that Amadeus sends is kept as Amadeus sends it. The OTA API refuses a card number in the free text that staff and customers type (`card_data`, FIX-W67-KI001 and FIX-W68-CARDTEXT), but a remark a terminal agent typed into the order, or the remarks of an imported or resynced order, are copied into `booking_remarks` (`orderRemarksOf` keeps each `text`), into `bookings.order_snapshot` and into the supplier log (`supplier_requests`). Those copies pass only the shared [[redact-payload]], which masks by key name (`cardNumber`, `pan`, a card's `number`), never by what a text holds. A card number in such a remark therefore reaches the tenant database and its backups. Accepted for now by lead decision (37e) and recorded as a residual risk in the PCI pack (`ota/docs/pci/README.md` §8 item 8).
reproduce: With the Amadeus stub, give an order a general remark whose text holds a test card number, for example `PAX CARD 4111 1111 1111 1111`.
Import it in the OTA admin (PNR import), or resync a booking whose order now carries that remark.
Read `tenant_<key>.booking_remarks.text`, the booking's `order_snapshot` and the import's `supplier_requests.response_body`: the number is there in full.
expected: A card number in supplier text never reaches the database whole: it is masked on receipt (as `holdsCardNumber` finds it) or the text is not stored.
actual: The remark text, the order snapshot and the supplier log keep the number as Amadeus sent it.
fix: A later decision (37e): mask card numbers in supplier free text on receipt with a `holdsCardNumber`-like masker in `orderRemarksOf`, `keptOrderDataOf`, the sync's snapshot and the supplier log, or refuse to store such a text. No code now; until then staff never type card data into an order at the airline's or Amadeus's terminal (PCI responsibility matrix row 3).

title: Becoming an owner never checks MAX_TENANTS_PER_ACCOUNT
summary: An account can own more OTAs than `MAX_TENANTS_PER_ACCOUNT` (default 3). `createTenant` and the owner's retry refuse with `422 UNPROCESSABLE` (`details.reason` `tenant_limit`) once the account owns that many OTAs that are not `failed`, but the two other ways to become an owner count nothing: accepting an invitation with the role `owner` (`InvitationsService.accept` inserts or reactivates the membership with the invitation's role) and `changeRole` to `owner` (`MembersService.changeRole` checks permissions, MFA and the version only).
reproduce: With `MAX_TENANTS_PER_ACCOUNT=1`, let account A own one active OTA.
As the owner of another OTA, invite A as `owner` (or invite A as `admin` and then change A's role to `owner`).
A accepts: A now owns two OTAs, and `createTenant` as A still answers `422 tenant_limit`.
expected: A rule for the limit when an account becomes an owner: either both paths refuse with the same `tenant_limit` error, or the limit is documented as counting only the OTAs an account creates.
actual: Both paths succeed whatever the account already owns; `listTenants` then answers a `tenantLimit.owned` above `max`, and the portal's dashboard names both numbers.
fix: A later decision (37k): count the account's owned OTAs that are not `failed` under the same row lock as `createTenant` in `accept` and in `changeRole` to `owner`, or write down in scope PF-10 that the limit applies to creating OTAs only. No code now.
